messages:
Tom (PM): Heads-up: we're starting a coordinated deprecation of blocking/synchronous SDK helpers across official SDKs. Goal is an async-first surface to improve throughput and compatibility with modern runtimes.
Sofia (SDK Eng): Short summary: we'll introduce an explicit `sync-compat` adapter package and deprecation warnings in v4.3, then remove sync helpers in v5.0 (~180 days).
Lina (Docs): Timeline request: can we keep both the async examples and a short sync migration section for the deprecation window? Customers rely on quickstarts.
Sofia (SDK Eng): Yes. Plan:
- v4.3 minor: add deprecation warning when sync helpers are constructed; publish `@redwood/sdk-sync-compat` / `redwood-sdk-sync` artifact concurrently.
- 90 days: recommend migration complete; add stronger logs in v4.6.
- v5.0 (major, ~180 days): remove sync helpers from main packages.
Priya (Developer Relations): We should prepare blog + migration webinar. Many users still use sync examples in README.
Tom (PM): Agreed. Action: docs to keep both codepaths with clear banners and a migration checklist. Lina, can you own sample updates?
Lina (Docs): Yup. I'll update quickstarts to show async-first examples and include a collapsible sync section that points to the compat package. Will also add a short FAQ for serverless users.
Ethan (QA): What about our sample apps and CI? Will tests break?
Sofia (SDK Eng): We'll publish the compat package as a thin shim that wraps async calls with a threadpool or an event-loop adapter depending on language. It won't be high-performance but will preserve compatibility. Internals will log a deprecation warning once per process.
Sofia (SDK Eng): Languages covered at launch: Python, Node (JS/TS), Go. Rust will get a separate RFC due to different async model.
Tom (PM): Migration snippets for docs: please include both languages. Lina, use these as canonical text.

Python (old sync):
```python
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.generate("Summarize my notes")
print(resp.text)

# new async-first
import asyncio
from redwood import InferenceClient

async def main():
    client = InferenceClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
    resp = await client.generate("Summarize my notes")
    print(resp.text)

asyncio.run(main())
```

JS (old sync-ish):
```javascript
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = client.generate("Summarize my notes"); // blocking helper
console.log(resp.text);

// new async-first
import Redwood from 'redwood';
const client = new Redwood.InferenceClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate("Summarize my notes");
console.log(resp.text);
```

Priya (Developer Relations): We'll surface the codemods for Python/JS that can rewrite common patterns. Dev Outreach will send a targeted email to accounts with heavy sync usage.
Sofia (SDK Eng): Compatibility notes:
- The compat package will be versioned independently so customers can pin it past v5.0 if absolutely needed.
- It will be clearly labeled: "not recommended for low-latency/high-throughput production".
- We'll add runtime telemetry when users opt-in so we can measure adoption.
Lina (Docs): Docs site behavior: during the deprecation window we'll show an interstitial banner on quickstarts and the top of SDK pages. We'll show both the async example first and a folded sync section.
Ethan (QA): I'll add tests that run sample apps with the compat package and assert deprecation warnings are emitted and no functional regressions.
dev-bot: RFC issue created: https://go.redwood/rfc/1745003210-sync-deprecation (assignee: @Sofia) :memo:
Tom (PM): Risks/concerns? Anything blocking the schedule?
Sofia (SDK Eng): Main risk: large orgs that vendor a frozen SDK copy. We'll coordinate a migration playbook and reach out to platform teams. Also need to verify packaging constraints for the compat artifact in our registries.
Priya (Developer Relations): Recommend a migration checklist for account teams: list of repos likely affected (based on usage telemetry), sample migration PRs, and an offer for engineering support for customers on paid tiers.
Lina (Docs): I'll draft the migration checklist and add a sample PR template. ETA EOD Friday for a draft.
Tom (PM): OK. I'll add this to the release notes draft and put a short blurb in next week's all-hands. If any teams need help identifying affected repos, ping me.
Sofia (SDK Eng): We'll open PRs for SDKs to add the deprecation messages and publish the compat packages on the same day v4.3 ships.
Lina (Docs): Thanks everyone. I'll keep the doc updated and link to the codemod repos.
Priya (Developer Relations): I'll prepare the comms cadence: announcement, migration guide, webinar, and follow-ups.
Ethan (QA): Adding a QA checklist to the release checklist now.
Sofia (SDK Eng): Final note: class/name change proposal in the RFC (InferenceClient rename) will be referenced here so users see the full migration surface.
Tom (PM): Great. Close loop: next check-in in #docs on Wednesday.
